flags.reason: Feature extraction reads every SPair test annotation's target keypoints and injects their density into image tokens, leaking held-out labels into evaluation.
The checkpoint is selected by maximizing point/All from a results metrics file, amounting to test-metric model selection for the sole provided evaluation.
The required conditioner module is absent even though util.py and sampling.py import HFEmbedder from it, so the evaluation cannot import in a fresh checkout.
Model loading unconditionally opens this absent file before any checkpoint fallback, and no repository code creates the expected metrics/checkpoint schema.
Features are split into unconditional/text halves although Featurizer4Eval creates only conditional ensemble samples; ensemble_size=1 in the supplied launcher makes tuple unpacking fail outright.
The parser's default double-stream layers [12,14] return only feature tensors, but the last tensor is treated as a modulation object and accessed via mod.shift/mod.scale.
DoubleStreamBlock always returns three values regardless of return_feat, while Flux.forward expects two, breaking the normal model forward path at its first double block.
SingleStreamBlock always returns a tuple regardless of return_feat, while Flux.forward assigns it to one tensor and would fail on the next block.

The shared timestep embedding uses 1000*(1-t), reversing the t convention used by the 1-to-0 sampler and noisy-latent interpolation and also nonsensically transforming guidance values through 1-guidance.
The function called attention never computes cross-token attention and instead gates each value against a 1-D average pool, contradicting the transformer's stated attention operation.
--guidance_scale is assigned but never used because the CFG formula is commented out and feature extraction always uses its separate hard-coded default guidance=3.5.
The advertised ensemble is never averaged; evaluation later discards one arbitrary half and uses only batch element zero, so ensemble_size does not implement ensembling.
Selecting more than one single-stream feature index interleaves ModulationOut objects with tensors, which Featurizer4Eval then tries to rearrange as feature tensors.
The src-layout package has neither setup.py nor pyproject.toml despite egg metadata listing both, while test_spair.sh neither installs it nor sets PYTHONPATH, so 'import flux' is not reproducible.
Spatial calibration ignores --dataset_path and reads a CWD-relative ./dataset/SPair-71k, so the same command silently changes behavior depending on an unrelated directory's presence.
Spatial calibration assumes the token count is a perfect square and reshapes side^2 values onto all tokens, so the evaluator's documented non-square image sizes cause a shape mismatch.
Double-stream blocks normalize each channel across tokens via TokenInstanceNorm while single-stream blocks use per-token LayerNorm, an unexplained architectural inconsistency for pretrained weights.
attention_map materializes an unused quadratic v-v matrix after a hard-coded 512-token offset, consuming roughly 2 GB per block at the default batch of eight and 768px input.
Result filenames depend only on guidance_scale, so runs with different timesteps, feature layers, image sizes, or ensemble sizes silently overwrite one another.
Evaluation samples both VAE latents and added noise without any seed or generator, making reported correspondence scores non-reproducible.
